outcome: The conjecture was proved before the window: Frohardt and Magaard's Annals paper (2001) states in its abstract that it proves the 1990 Guralnick–Thompson conjecture on composition factors of monodromy groups, which includes the genus-0 case the bullet names. No event dated after 26 January 2024 bears on that question. The post-window events concern neighbouring questions (monodromy groups of bounded-genus covers, type-B primitive groups in genus 0 and 1, polynomial monodromy) or a different conjecture that also goes by Thompson's name.
problem_asks: (1) The groups G occurring in genus-0 systems: transitive permutation groups generated by elements satisfying a genus-0 Riemann–Hurwitz-type index condition (Aschbacher 1990 formalism); by Riemann's existence theorem these are monodromy groups of covers of the Riemann sphere by genus-0 curves. (2) The composition factors of those groups. (3) The conjectured claim the bullet names: that the nonabelian, non-alternating simple composition factors of such groups form a finite set. The frozen wording says only 'conjecture on the composition factors'; the literature version excludes alternating groups and cyclic groups of prime order (Guralnick–Thompson 1990; Thompson's genus-0 phrasing as quoted in Shih 1991: apart from Zₚ and Aₖ with k≥5, only finitely many simple groups are composition factors of genus-0 groups). (4) Not asked by the bullet's wording, but part of the general conjecture: the same finiteness for every genus g. (5) Possible further reading: the explicit list of the exceptional groups, which is part of Thompson's genus-0 programme but not the conjecture's stated claim.

events.what_happened: Robert Guralnick and John G. Thompson, 'Finite groups of genus zero', J. Algebra 131 (1990) 303–341, which formulates the conjecture that for each genus g the set E*(g) of nonabelian non-alternating composition factors of monodromy groups of genus-g covers is finite. The original form asks that for each q, apart from finitely many simple groups, only alternating and cyclic groups occur as composition factors of monodromy groups of covers of the projective line. Not opened: the paper and its Caltech resolver page (which redirected) were not read; the statement comes from search snippets.
events.delivers: Formulates the conjecture only. From the snippets it establishes no finiteness result of its own, so it settles no part of problem_asks.
events.direction: Poses the conjectured finiteness, which is the claim the bullet asks about.

events.what_happened: Michael Aschbacher, 'On conjectures of Guralnick and Thompson', J. Algebra 135(2) (1990) 277–343, DOI 10.1016/0021-8693(90)90292-V. The frozen Wikipedia bullet cites it as reference [24]. The Caltech record, which I opened, gives the abstract's first sentences: for a permutation s it defines c(s) and Ind(s) = n − c(s), and a genus-g system as a triple (G, Ω, S) with G transitive on Ω, S a generating family of non-identity elements with product 1, and an index equation relating |Ω| and g. The abstract states no theorem. ScienceDirect returned 403 and the Elsevier redirect did not resolve, so the full text was not read.
events.delivers: Unknown. What I could read defines genus-g systems and states no result. I cannot say whether it proves anything about composition factors of genus-0 systems, or whether it is the source of the bullet's genus-0 wording.
events.direction: Unknown from the abstract. The title and the Wikipedia citation tie it to the Guralnick–Thompson conjecture.

events.what_happened: Tanchu Shih, PhD dissertation, Caltech 1991, 'Bounds of fixed point ratios of permutation representations of GL_n(q) and groups of genus zero' (advisor Aschbacher). For primitive G with Lₙ(q) ≤ G ≤ PGL_n(q) the main theorem says a genus-zero group satisfies one of: q=2 with n≤32; q=3 with n≤12; q=4 with n≤11; 5≤q≤13 with n≤8; 16≤q≤83 with n≤4; 89≤q≤343 with n=2. The abstract says this confirms J. Thompson's conjecture (finitely many simple composition factors of genus-zero groups apart from Zₚ and Aₖ, k≥5) for this family. Only the abstract page was read.
events.delivers: For primitive G between Lₙ(q) and PGL_n(q), a genus-zero G must have (q, n) in the finite list above, so the composition factors of genus-zero groups in this type-A family lie in finitely many simple groups. Restricted to the linear type-A sandwich; says nothing about other Lie types or other primitive types.
events.remains: Simple groups outside the sandwich Lₙ(q) ≤ G ≤ PGL_n(q), and every other primitive type; so the full claim of problem_asks.

checked_by.qualification: Aschbacher is a leading finite group theorist; the committee's own qualifications were not read
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted the dissertation for the Caltech PhD. The thesis record exists; the committee's review is not visible in what I read.

events.doubts: The 2025 Gerhardt–McKemmie–Neftin paper says Shih's type-B genus-0 argument had 'a few small gaps'. That concerns primitive groups with more than one minimal normal subgroup, not the type-A bounds recorded here, so I do not carry it over to this event.
events.direction: Cuts toward finiteness, for the linear type-A family only.

events.what_happened: Daniel Frohardt and Kay Magaard, 'Composition factors of monodromy groups', Annals of Mathematics 154 (2001), no. 2, 327–345, DOI 10.2307/3062099. The abstract, which I opened, says: 'The authors prove the 1990 conjecture of Guralnick and Thompson on composition factors of monodromy groups.' The page does not state the theorem. Secondary sources (snippets, not opened) describe the method: Riemann's existence theorem turns the problem into one about primitive permutation groups; that is reduced to classical groups acting on subspaces of natural modules; the tools are fixed-point-ratio estimates from the authors' earlier work and a generation result of Scott. The same snippets state the conjecture as E*(g) finite for each g, excluding alternating groups and cyclic groups of prime order. Dating: the Annals gives 2001; one search snippet says the proof was completed in 1999. I record 2001 as the only documented date and flag the 1999 claim as unverified.
events.revisions: One search snippet says the proof was completed in 1999. No preprint version was found in my searches.
events.delivers: Proves the 1990 Guralnick–Thompson conjecture: for every genus g the set E*(g) of nonabelian, non-alternating simple composition factors of monodromy groups of genus-g covers is finite. This gives finiteness of the genus-0 set provided g = 0 is included and genus-0 systems are the same objects as monodromy groups of genus-0 covers. The first point is supported by the abstract's reading of the conjecture and by Aschbacher's definition of genus-g systems; the second rests on a snippet claim that the genus-0 set lies inside E*(g) for every g. Neither is stated in the abstract, and I did not read the theorem.
events.remains: Nothing on the finiteness question if the theorem covers g = 0 as the snippets say. Not determined: the explicit list of exceptional groups, which finiteness alone does not give. Also unverified: whether the Annals statement is explicit for g = 0, and whether it matches the bullet's 'genus-0 systems' wording.

checked_by.qualification: Co-originator of the 1990 conjecture; leading researcher on monodromy groups
checked_by.what_they_did: Describes the Frohardt–Magaard theorem as completing the final step in resolving the conjecture, in a 2003 MSRI expository chapter. Known only from a search snippet; the PDF was unreadable to me, so this is not a checked reading.

checked_by.qualification: Researcher on fixed point ratios and simple groups
checked_by.what_they_did: A 2017 arXiv survey (1707.03564) reportedly states the finiteness theorem for each genus as established. Known only from a search snippet; the PDF was unreadable and the ar5iv render stopped before the relevant section.

checked_by.who: Danny Neftin and Michael E. Zieve
checked_by.qualification: Researchers on monodromy groups of covers
checked_by.what_they_did: Cite Frohardt–Magaard in the proof of their Theorem 1.1 (2024 arXiv preprint). This is use of the result, not an independent check of the 2001 argument.

events.direction: Proves the conjectured finiteness, in the direction the bullet's conjecture points.

events.what_happened: Michael D. Fried, 'Relating two genus 0 problems of John Thompson', arXiv:0910.3974 (20 Oct 2009); a search snippet says it appears in Progress in Galois Theory (Thompson's 70th birthday volume, pp. 51–85). The abstract, which I opened, relates three problems: Davenport's problem; showing that monodromy groups of rational function maps over C are limited to a finite set of groups; and relating genus-0 modular curves to Monstrous Moonshine. It poses problems and states no result on composition factors.
events.delivers: Establishes nothing on composition factors. Poses the genus-0 monodromy problem (finitely many primitive genus-0 monodromy groups beyond the alternating, symmetric, cyclic and dihedral families) as a target. That is a question about monodromy groups, not composition factors.
events.remains: All of problem_asks, and the genus-0 monodromy problem the paper poses.
events.direction: Poses the problem; no result cutting either way.

events.what_happened: Michael D. Fried, 'Variables separated equations: Strikingly different roles for the Branch Cycle Lemma and the Finite Simple Group Classification', arXiv:1012.5297 (v1 23 Dec 2010; last revised 11 Aug 2011). The abstract, which I opened, says: 'This encouraged J. Thompson to formulate the genus 0 problem on rational function monodromy groups. R. Guralnick and Thompson led its solution in stages.' The body was not read.
events.delivers: An expository abstract describing the genus-0 monodromy-group problem as solved by Guralnick and Thompson in stages. The paper's own content (Davenport's problem, the Branch Cycle Lemma, the classification) is not the composition-factor claim. The abstract gives no dates and no precise scope.
events.remains: All of problem_asks, as far as the abstract shows.
events.direction: A status statement about the genus-0 monodromy-group problem (solved in stages). I did not verify a theorem list behind it.

events.what_happened: Kay Magaard, Sergey Shpectorov and Gehao Wang, 'Generating sets of affine groups of low genus', arXiv:1108.4833 (24 Aug 2011). The abstract, which I opened, describes a new algorithm for braid orbits on Nielsen classes, applied to classify all families of affine genus-zero systems, i.e. coverings of the Riemann sphere whose monodromy group is a primitive affine permutation group.
events.delivers: Classifies genus-0 systems whose monodromy group is primitive affine. Restricted to the affine subclass; does not address the non-affine genus-0 systems the bullet concerns.
events.remains: Non-affine genus-0 systems, and so the rest of problem_asks.
events.direction: Classification of the affine subclass; no direction on the conjectured finiteness.

events.what_happened: Daniel Frohardt, Robert Guralnick and Kay Magaard, 'Primitive monodromy groups of genus at most two', arXiv:1401.1303 (submitted 7 Jan 2014); a search snippet says it appeared in J. Algebra in 2014. The abstract, which I opened, says that if a classical group acts on a set Ω of 1-spaces of its natural module with genus at most two, then |Ω| ≤ 10,000.
events.delivers: A degree bound, |Ω| ≤ 10,000, for one restricted family of genus-≤2 primitive actions (classical groups on 1-spaces). Not a composition-factor result for genus-0 systems.
events.remains: All of problem_asks; the paper states no composition-factor finiteness result.
events.direction: Degree bound within a restricted family; no direction on the conjectured finiteness.

events.what_happened: Danny Neftin and Michael E. Zieve, 'Monodromy groups of indecomposable coverings of bounded genus', arXiv:2403.17167 (25 Mar 2024; single version). The abstract, which I opened, says it classifies, for each nonnegative integer g, the ramification types and monodromy groups of indecomposable complex covers f: X→Y with genus(X) = g, when the degree is sufficiently large and the monodromy group is not Aₙ or Sₙ, and that this 'proves a conjecture of Guralnick and several conjectures of Guralnick and Shareshian'. Theorem 1.1 has a constant N_g, and genus-0 cases appear explicitly (g_X = 0 in cases (2) and (4)). The introduction, read in the HTML up to about 100,000 of about 156,000 characters, records that earlier work already yields a classification of the simple composition factors of large-degree indecomposable covers, and that applications need the full monodromy group. Proposition A.1 proves eight of ten assertions of Guralnick–Shareshian Conjecture 3.29, with Remark 4.2 covering the other two (a snippet; not opened).
events.revisions: Single version v1, 25 Mar 2024, per the arXiv listing.
events.delivers: A full monodromy-group classification for indecomposable covers of genus g with degree at least N_g and monodromy group not Aₙ or Sₙ, for every g including g = 0. Its composition-factor consequence was already available from earlier work, according to its introduction. It does not settle finiteness of composition factors for genus-0 systems in general, because it applies only above the degree bound N_g and only to indecomposable covers.
events.remains: Covers of degree below N_g and decomposable covers. The paper does not claim anything new about composition factors.
events.direction: Cuts toward classification, including genus-0 cases, and does not contradict the conjectured finiteness.

events.what_happened: Danny Neftin and Michael E. Zieve, 'Monodromy groups of product type', arXiv:2403.17168 (25 Mar 2024; single version), companion to 2403.17167. The abstract, which I opened, says: 'The combination of this paper and its companion complete the classification of monodromy groups of indecomposable coverings of complex curves f:X→P¹ of sufficiently large degree in comparison to the genus of X.' Theorem 1.2, read in the HTML up to about 100,000 of about 141,000 characters, covers t ≥ 2 and G of product type in S_ℓ ≀ S_t: either g_X > c·ℓ^(t−1) − d·ℓ^(t−2), or the ramification type is in Table 3.1. Table cases have t = 2, base curve of genus 0, and g_X ≤ 1. The acknowledgements thank Robert Guralnick for helpful comments; that is not a verification.
events.revisions: Single version v1, 25 Mar 2024, per the arXiv listing.
events.delivers: Determines all indecomposable coverings whose monodromy group is of product type, for sufficiently large degree relative to genus. Together with 2403.17167 it completes the classification the authors describe. Composition factors are not discussed in the parts I read.
events.remains: Non-product-type groups are handled by 2403.17167. Nothing new on composition-factor finiteness is established.
events.direction: Classification side; no contradiction of finiteness.

events.what_happened: Spencer Gerhardt, Eilidh McKemmie and Danny Neftin, 'Low-genus primitive monodromy groups with a nonunique minimal normal subgroup', arXiv:2501.15538 (v1 26 Jan 2025; v2 16 Jul 2025). The introduction, which I opened in full, says Shih determined the type-B monodromy groups of genus-0 indecomposable covers up to a few small gaps, and that the paper closes them by extending Shih's argument, 'thereby completing the classification of type-B monodromy groups'. Main Theorem 1, for genus below max{2, n/5000}: for g ≤ 1 there is exactly one such covering, with n = 168 and G ≅ PSL₂(7)²·C₂; for arbitrary g there are none once n is large in terms of g. Publication: Communications in Algebra 54(4), pp. 1698–1707 (2026), per the Kean University research record, which I opened; the journal page itself was not opened.
events.revisions: v1 26 Jan 2025; v2 16 Jul 2025 (current version per the arXiv listing).
events.delivers: Completes the classification of type-B primitive monodromy groups of indecomposable covers in genus 0 and 1: one covering, n = 168, G ≅ PSL₂(7)²·C₂, for g ≤ 1; for arbitrary genus, none once n is large in terms of g. Restricted to the type-B class, meaning more than one minimal normal subgroup. Says nothing about type-A or other primitive types.
events.remains: Other primitive types and composition factors of general genus-0 systems. Whether the large-n condition is sharp is not addressed in what I read.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper, per the Kean University research record (volume 54, issue 4, pp. 1698–1707, 2026). I did not open the journal's own page and saw no referee information.

events.direction: Classification side for type-B groups: one exceptional covering in genus ≤ 1, none for large degree. No contradiction of finiteness.
events.object: The unique type-B covering in the genus ≤ 1 range: degree n = 168, monodromy group G ≅ PSL₂(7)²·C₂, as stated in the main theorem. Whether it is explicit or was located by computation is not stated in the parts I read; the acknowledgements mention GAP and MAGMA calculations.

events.what_happened: Angelot Behajaina, Joachim König and Danny Neftin, 'Monodromy groups of polynomials of composition length 2', arXiv:2603.27609 (submitted 29 Mar 2026; v2 31 Jul 2026). The abstract, which I opened, says that the monodromy groups of compositions of two indecomposable polynomials either have a 'largeness' property or lie in an explicit list of exceptions, and that the result is a key ingredient in solving a Davenport–Lewis–Schinzel problem in a companion paper, which I did not locate.
events.delivers: Structure of full monodromy groups of two-step polynomial compositions. Polynomials are genus-0 covers with one totally ramified point, so this is a restricted class, and the result concerns full monodromy groups rather than finiteness of composition factors of genus-0 systems.
events.direction: Neither direction on the conjecture; a structural result on a special class.

events.what_happened: Jun Liao, Lizhong Wang and Jiping Zhang, 'Thompson's Conjecture for Finite Simple Groups of Lie Type over Small Fields', arXiv:2608.17891 (submitted 18 Aug 2026; v1 only). The abstract and introduction, which I opened in part, state the Thompson conjecture here as the class-squares statement: every nonabelian finite simple group G has a conjugacy class C with C² = G. The paper claims a proof for Lie-type groups over fields of order at most 8 and says that with earlier cases it completes Thompson's conjecture. This is a different problem from the bullet. An AI-use acknowledgement (ChatGPT for exploring proof strategies; GAP and Python for character calculations; AI tools for English editing; AI-suggested steps independently verified) appears only in a search snippet. The acknowledgements were not visible in the HTML I read, and the PDF was unreadable.
events.delivers: Claims the class-squares conjecture for Lie-type groups over fields of order ≤ 8. That is a different conjecture from the genus-0 composition-factor question and establishes nothing for the bullet.
events.remains: All of problem_asks; this paper is not about it.
events.direction: Positive for the class-squares conjecture, as claimed. No direction on the bullet.

events.what_happened: Ohad Sheinfeld, 'On Shalev's Quantitative Version of Thompson's Conjecture', arXiv:2609.22004 (submitted 18 Sep 2026; v1 only). The abstract, which I opened, says Shalev's stronger quantitative form of the class-squares Thompson conjecture fails in general. The paper proves a close variant over PSL_n(2) for large n, gives counterexamples over PSL_n(8) and PSL_n(5), and disproves a conjecture of Pyber. Neither the abstract nor the introduction I read mentions genus-0 covers or composition factors of monodromy groups. The acknowledgements, read in the HTML v1, credit AI systems (see ai).
events.delivers: Counterexamples to Shalev's quantitative version of the Thompson class-squares conjecture, and a close variant for PSL_n(2) for large n. Not the bullet's question.
events.doubts: The acknowledgements say the first proof of the main theorem and the counterexamples were produced by AI systems. The parts I read contain no statement that the authors checked those outputs by hand. This concerns the neighbouring conjecture, not the bullet.
events.direction: Counterexamples against Shalev's quantitative version. The classical class-squares statement is not claimed to fail.
events.object: Counterexamples: for PSL_n(8), conjugacy classes for which SS⁻¹ misses even elements of support size linear in n (abstract). For PSL_n(5), an inverse-closed normal set for every odd n ≥ 5 (HTML abstract). Whether the constructions are explicit is not stated in the parts I read.

systems.basis_quote: A first version of the proof of the main theorem was obtained through interactive sessions with ChatGPT 5.6 and Gemini 3.1. In addition, the counterexamples were constructed entirely by these AI systems.

disputes.summary: Completion year of the Frohardt–Magaard proof: 1999 in one search snippet (source not opened), 2001 in the Annals listing and in later snippets. Unresolved; I recorded 2001. The window is unaffected either way.

'Thompson's conjecture' names several different problems in the sources: the genus-0 composition-factor problem (Shih 1991; Fried), the class-squares conjecture (Liao–Wang–Zhang 2026; Sheinfeld 2026), and a 1987/88 same-class-sizes problem (snippet only). The 2026 AI-acknowledged papers concern the class-squares problem, not this bullet.

Authorship of the genus-0 problem: Fried's 2010 abstract says Thompson formulated the genus-0 problem and that 'R. Guralnick and Thompson led its solution in stages'. The frozen bullet's source [24] (Aschbacher 1990) and the 1990 paper name Guralnick and Thompson for the composition-factor conjecture. Recorded for the judging pass; not a priority dispute as such.

summary: The conjecture (Guralnick and Thompson, J. Algebra 1990) asks that the nonabelian, non-alternating composition factors of monodromy groups of genus-g covers form a finite set E*(g). The Annals abstract for Frohardt and Magaard (2001) says the paper proves this conjecture. The genus-0 case is the frozen bullet's question. I read only the abstract on the Annals page, not the theorem, so whether the statement explicitly includes g = 0 and matches the bullet's exclusions is unverified. A search snippet says the genus-0 set lies inside E*(g) for every g, which would carry the general theorem down to genus 0. The frozen bullet cites Aschbacher (1990), 'On conjectures of Guralnick and Thompson', as reference [24]. I could read only Aschbacher's abstract, which defines genus-g systems and states no theorem, so what he proved is unknown to me. Shih's 1991 Caltech thesis gives a genus-0 classification for Lₙ(q) ≤ G ≤ PGL_n(q) with a finite list of (q, n), and its abstract says it confirms Thompson's version for that family. That is a restricted, pre-window case. Fried (2009, 2010) treats the genus-0 monodromy-group problem for primitive groups, a different question; the 2010 abstract says Guralnick and Thompson 'led its solution in stages'. Since the window opened, Neftin and Zieve (March 2024, arXiv 2403.17167 and companion 2403.17168) classify monodromy groups of indecomposable covers of each genus for large degree, including genus 0. Their introduction says the composition-factor classification for such covers was already available, so they add no finiteness result for composition factors. Gerhardt, McKemmie and Neftin (arXiv 2501.15538, January 2025) complete the type-B primitive classification for genus 0 and 1: one covering, degree 168, G ≅ PSL₂(7)²·C₂. That concerns one primitive type, not composition factors of general genus-0 systems. Behajaina, König and Neftin (arXiv 2603.27609, March 2026) study monodromy groups of polynomials of composition length 2, which is neighbouring. The Thompson class-squares papers of 2026 (Liao–Wang–Zhang; Sheinfeld) are not about this bullet. Sheinfeld's acknowledgements credit ChatGPT 5.6, Gemini 3.1 and ChatGPT Astra with a first proof of the main theorem, the counterexamples and a simplification; I read this in the HTML, but the quotes come through the fetch tool's extraction and are not checked byte-for-byte. Liao–Wang–Zhang's AI credit appears only in a search snippet and is unverified. No source ties an AI system to the Guralnick–Thompson conjecture itself. The AI-specific searches (the conjecture's name with AI terms, Frohardt–Magaard, genus-zero monodromy, Lean formalisation, lab announcements and trackers) found nothing relevant. Several pre-2024 partial results (Liebeck–Saxl, Liebeck–Shalev 1999, Neubauer, Guralnick–Neubauer) and Guralnick's 2003 MSRI survey are known only from snippets, so I did not record them as events.
competing_reading: The bullet could be asking for the explicit list of groups in genus-0 systems, not just finiteness. On that reading the 2001 theorem gives finiteness without the list. The list is still incomplete: Shih (1991) covers only the type-A family with bounded (q, n), Fried (2009) calls the genus-0 problem 'nearly proven' (snippet from his own page, not opened), and the 2025 paper covers only type-B groups. A second reading: 'genus-0 systems' in the bullet means Aschbacher's combinatorial systems, which may be a larger class than monodromy groups of genus-0 covers. If so, Frohardt–Magaard's statement about monodromy groups would not cover the bullet verbatim, and Aschbacher's 1990 paper, which the bullet cites, would need to be read.
what_would_settle_it: (a) The Annals theorem statement: whether it is explicit for g = 0 and what exclusions it uses. (b) Aschbacher 1990's main results, and whether 'genus-0 system' there matches monodromy groups of genus-0 covers. (c) The 1999 versus 2001 completion date, from the authors' preprint or the Annals submission history. (d) The wording of the bullet's own source [24] and what the bullet is taken to ask: finiteness, or the explicit list. (e) The end of Neftin–Zieve 2403.17167, to confirm the AI-use statement, and whether their Theorem 1.1 changes any genus-0 composition-factor statement.
